target.title: test(infra): add unit tests for semver comparison helpers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/infra/semver-compare.ts` had **no test coverage**, yet its four exported helpers decide real version ordering in six call sites — `update-check.ts` (is an update available), `clawhub.ts`, `update-channels.ts`, `config/version.ts`, and `plugins/install.ts` / `plugins/update.ts` (which bundled/installed plugin wins). A regression in `parseComparableSemver`, prerelease precedence, or build-metadata handling would silently pick the wrong version — e.g. serve a prerelease as newer than its stable release, or mis-order `1.2.11` vs `1.2.9` — with no test to catch it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a focused, table-driven suite (`src/infra/semver-compare.test.ts`) that pins the current, correct behavior of all four exports:

- `normalizeLegacyDotBetaVersion` — legacy `1.2.3.beta.N` → `1.2.3-beta.N`, `v`/`V` prefixes, and passthrough for already-semver / non-matching strings.
- `parseComparableSemver` — stable/prerelease parsing, `v` prefix, dotted and hyphenated prerelease identifiers, build-metadata stripping, the opt-in legacy normalization, zero components, and `null` for every malformed shape (too few/many segments, non-numeric, empty, `null`/`undefined`).
- `comparePrereleaseIdentifiers` — the full semver 2.0.0 precedence rules: stable > prerelease, numeric-vs-numeric compared numerically (`2 < 11`, not lexically), numeric < alphanumeric, ASCII order for alphanumerics, and larger-set-outranks-smaller when the shared prefix is equal.
- `compareComparableSemver` — core major/minor/patch ordering, build-metadata independence, prerelease-below-release, and `null` when either side is unparsable.

It also encodes the **canonical semver.org §11 precedence chain** (`1.0.0-alpha < …-alpha.1 < …-alpha.beta < …-beta < …-beta.2 < …-beta.11 < …-rc.1 < 1.0.0`) as a documented regression anchor.

This is **test-only** — no production code is touched. Before writing the suite I drove the real functions against the full spec chain and edge cases to confirm current `main` is spec-correct, so these assertions lock in verified behavior rather than a guess.

## User Impact

None at runtime. Developer-facing: version-ordering logic that drives update and plugin-install decisions is now guarded against silent regressions.

## Evidence

`vitest run src/infra/semver-compare.test.ts`:

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  47 passed (47)
```

Every assertion is derived from the semver 2.0.0 spec (numeric-before-alphanumeric precedence, shorter-set-lower, build-metadata ignored) and the semver.org §11 example ordering. oxlint and `oxfmt --check` are clean; `it.each` tables are explicitly typed so `check-test-types` stays green.
